note.question: When will competing firms voluntarily share proprietary R&D data, and when do their sharing incentives underor overshoot the innovation-maximizing government policy?
note.overview: The voluntary-sharing model explicitly solves a symmetric pure-strategy Bayesian Nash equilibrium among competing R&D firms; the government case is a centralized benchmark.

components.label: Symmetric pure-strategy Bayesian Nash equilibrium under voluntary data sharing
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Symmetric pure-strategy Bayesian Nash equilibrium under voluntary data sharing. Proposition 1 on PDF p. 9 establishes a symmetric pure-strategy Bayesian Nash equilibrium and characterizes effort and sharing; the authors explicitly state that uniqueness is not required. Propositions 2-3 on PDF pp. 11-12 compare voluntary sharing with the centralized benchmark and show that intervention is not uniformly pro-sharing.
